answer: Epoch-linked behavioural fingerprint. Each identity must carry a rolling policy signature across a fixed horizon of past epochs; a new identity inherits no history and must run a probationary glacier phase where its actions are weighted near zero until the signature stabilises. Attackers forging N identities pay N full warm-up sequences, each requiring sustained low-value participation before any weight accrues. Sybils collapse because consistency is checked against prior epochs, not declarations. Cost: linear in identities times probation length, with opal-grade traceability of divergence.
